body:
# Ꜣst: the restoration, the temple, and the world it opens
Every name in this series was once flattened to fit a keyboard. **Ꜣst** is what the evidence put back.

Isis's mythology is the central drama of the Osirian cycle: love, murder, fragmentation, and restoration. It is also a handbook of magical power, because Isis does not accept loss as final. When Set dismembers Osiris and scatters his body across Egypt, Ꜣst wanders the land in mourning, gathering the pieces with her sister Nephthys.  She reassembles them, anoints the body, and, by her magic, conceives Horus.

That is the figure this file is about — and the temple now standing at its restored name.
## At a Glance

- **Restored name:** Ꜣst
- **ASCII form:** isis
- **Meaning:** "Throne (Egyptian ꜣst)"
- **Domain of influence:** Magic, Motherhood, Throne
- **Pantheon:** Egyptian
- **Classification:** Tier 1
- **Original script:** 𓊨𓏏𓆇
- **Series:** The Restoration Files, No. 119 of 271
## The Name Before the Marks

**Ꜣst** preserves its form without added diacritics: the restoration here is the exactness of the spelling itself, the form the tradition's own sources record. *isis* and **Ꜣst** may look interchangeable to a search box; they are not interchangeable to a philologist.
## The Temple That Stands Now

The restored name is not a plaque; it is an address. The temple of **Ꜣst** lives at [/sites/isis/](/sites/isis/), with its mythology in the [lore halls](/sites/isis/lore/), its peer-reviewed record in the [Scholarly Edition](/sites/isis/scholars/), and its place in the pattern atlas on the [patterns floor](/sites/isis/patterns/).

The restoration preserves more than the ASCII form can say — stress, length, or a letter the Latin keyboard lost — which places it in Tier-1: mechanically verifiable, information-rich.

Every flagship temple is hand-built to the same standard: the original script displayed with its provenance, the pronunciation reconstructed phoneme by phoneme, the sources named — because a restoration you cannot audit is just a spelling with confidence.
## The Archetype at Work

A temple is also a reading of what this figure *means* — and meanings have addresses in the modern world. The [pattern atlas](/patterns/) maps **Ꜣst** to the industries its archetype genuinely resonates with, each match argued, weighted, and open to challenge:

- **Leadership, Governance & Public Administration** — The throne personified; she seats and unseats kings.
- **Women's Health & Femtech** — Motherhood and magic; the complete feminine archetype.
- **Healthcare, Pharma & Medicine** — Healing magic and maternal care together.

The mapping is conservative on purpose: only resonances that can be argued aloud. The rest of the atlas follows the same rule, industry by industry.
## In the Sacred Texts

The Egyptian tradition is not a vibe; it is a library. The [Sacred Texts collection](/texts/) holds [The Book of the Dead](/texts/book-of-the-dead/) — the primary sources the temple's scholarship is built on, free to read, cross-linked back to the names they mention. The temple is the argument; the texts are the evidence.
## The File Continues

This is one of 271 Restoration Files — a second dispatch from every flagship temple in the fleet. The temple's [first dispatch](/sites/isis/blog/) tells the founding story of the name; the [blog index](/blog/) holds the whole archive.

Continue the series — previous file: **Ištar** ([read it here](/sites/ishtar/blog/restoration/)) · next file: **Ītzpāpālōtl** ([read it here](/sites/itzpapalotl/blog/restoration/)).

*The Restoration Files are written from the same canonical record as the temples themselves: the lexicon, the lore catalog, the pattern atlas, and the cited scholarly sources. If a file ever disagrees with its temple, the temple is right — tell us, and the file will be corrected.*
